column1: # Comparisons `constant-time-gate.sh` flags that are not timing oracles.
# One entry per line, three TAB-separated fields:
#   path<TAB>the source line, whitespace-trimmed<TAB>why it is not a timing oracle
# An entry is matched on its path and its exact line text, never on a line
# number. An entry that matches no line fails the gate: delete it with the line
# it excused. The preferred fix for a new hit is `subtle::ConstantTimeEq`, not
# a new entry; an entry is for a comparison whose operands are public, or whose
# timing reveals nothing an attacker does not already hold.

column3: A length check against a public constant: every wrapped blob is the same length, so the length is not secret.
The BIP-39 checksum of the phrase the caller typed. Both operands derive from that input alone, so the timing tells the caller nothing they did not type.
Test code inside #[cfg(test)] mod tests, asserting the signing secret never appears in an encoded payload. It runs on fixtures, never on attacker input.
